EP2 receptors mediate PGE1 stimulation of Na,K,ATPase beta 1 subunit gene transcription, and that EP1 receptors are involved in the PGE2 mediated inhibition of beta1 subunit gene expression.
EP1 and EP4 receptors are involved in the regulation of Na,K- ATPase beta subunit transcription by PGE1 in MDCK cells.

the regulation of the transcription of the beta1 subunit of the Na,K ATPase in MDCK cells by prostaglandin E1 and E2.
the regulation of ion transport by prostaglandin receptors.
identifying the EP receptors and the signal transduction mechanisms that regulate Na,K-ATpase gene transcription.

PGE1 stimulates Na,K-ATPa se beta1 subunit gene transcription via the EP1 and EP 2 receptors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EP1 and EP1 receptors are involved in the PGE mediated regulation of the Na, K ATPase in MDCK cells.

PGE2 and PGE1, through their EP2 and EP1 receptors respectively, stimulate the Na,K- ATPase beta subunit promoter in a manner that involves PKA and PKC signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

EP1 and EP1/EP2 receptors regulate the Na,K- ATPase in MDCK cells, but that EP1 and/or EP2 receptor activation is not sufficient to regulate the Na,K ATPase, since the EP1 and EP3 receptor agonists, 17-phenl trinor PGI2, and ONO-AE1-259, respectively, have no effect on Na,K-ATPAse expression.
the regulation of the transcription of the beta subunit gene of the Na,K ATPase is mediated by both EP1 and EP 2 receptors.
